name: ETP PostgreSQL
description: ETP infrastructure capability for PostgreSQL 17 relational database connectivity. Documents JDBC consumption, database-per-application isolation, deployment conventions, and operations. Not a runtime ETP service or SQL proxy.

version.description: Initial infrastructure capability documenting PostgreSQL 17, JDBC direct connectivity, Flyway-on-consumer pattern, and existing local Docker Compose references. Excludes REST APIs, automatic provisioning, and UAM implementation.

functional.summary: PostgreSQL 17 relational database infrastructure for ETP platform metadata, capability services, and application databases. Not a JVM runtime service or SQL proxy.
provides: PostgreSQL 17 database server (Docker image postgres:17 in local development)
PostgreSQL wire protocol and JDBC connectivity for consumer applications
Database-per-service/application isolation pattern (separate database names; separate containers in current local dev)
doesNotProvide: ETP REST APIs for SQL or database administration
Application schema design or Flyway migrations (consumer-owned)
Automatic application database provisioning (future platform scope)
Connection brokering or query proxy in the ETP runtime path

currentConsumersInRepository.purpose: Platform metadata (capability catalog, customers, applications, audit)

jdbc.driver: org.postgresql.Driver (PostgreSQL JDBC driver via Spring Boot dependency management)
jdbc.timezoneOption: Consumers set session timezone UTC (e.g. Hikari options or JDBC URL options=-c TimeZone=UTC)
jdbc.integration: Applications configure Spring Boot spring.datasource.* and connect directly — no ETP PostgreSQL middleware

documentation.note: Infrastructure capability — no OpenAPI service surface

credentials: Database username and password supplied via environment variables or secret manager
Never store live credentials in the Capability Registry contract document or registration payload
secretReferences: Production: secret manager / platform secret injection (deployment-specific)
networkAccess: Local development: PostgreSQL ports published via Docker Compose (examples: 5434 platform, 55432 IAM)
Non-dev: restrict database port exposure to application network; not configured in repository defaults
applicationIsolation: Dedicated database per service/application (etp_platform, etp_iam — not shared)
Current local dev uses separate PostgreSQL containers for platform and IAM
Default schema: public (PostgreSQL default); isolation is at database level, not separate PostgreSQL schemas per app

tlsSsl.detail: Current JDBC URLs use plain jdbc:postgresql:// without sslmode. TLS is a deployment responsibility for non-dev environments.

limitations: Single application database user per deployment in current examples (etp_admin)
No separate migration vs runtime DB user split in current Spring configuration
pgAdmin included in IAM docker-compose for dev convenience only — not part of capability runtime

deployment.implementationModel: Infrastructure container — not an ETP Spring Boot artifact
environmentSpecific: Docker Compose (local development — implemented in repository)
Kubernetes, AWS RDS, Azure Database for PostgreSQL (deployment-specific — not defined in repository)
deployment.databaseEndpoint: Host and port from deployment environment (JDBC URL)
deployment.databaseName: Per-consumer database name (e.g. etp_platform, etp_iam, future etp_uam)
deployment.schema: public (default PostgreSQL schema unless consumer configures otherwise)
deployment.persistentStorage: Docker named volumes in local compose (etp_platform_pgdata, etp-postgres-data)

nfr.connectionReliability: Consumer applications require a reachable PostgreSQL instance before Flyway and Hibernate validate succeed on startup
nfr.healthReadiness: Container health via pg_isready (platform compose); consumer readiness via JDBC connection.isValid in Spring Actuator health contributors
nfr.connectionPool: HikariCP via Spring Boot defaults in current consumers — no custom pool sizing in repository configuration
operationalRequirements: Start PostgreSQL before Flyway-enabled consumer services
No numeric latency or availability SLOs defined in repository for v1.0.0

startup: Create database and application user (manual, compose env, or operator)
Start consumer application (Flyway migrations run on consumer startup)
readiness: PostgreSQL: pg_isready (Docker healthcheck on platform container)
Consumers: Spring Boot Actuator db health and custom DatabaseConnectivityHealthIndicator (platform-service, etp-iam)
operations.databaseConnectivity: Verified by consumer JDBC pool, not by a dedicated ETP PostgreSQL service

migrations.framework: Flyway (Spring Boot integration in platform-service and etp-iam)
migrations.postgresCapabilityRole: Provides database server only — does not run application migrations

operations.environmentConfiguration: Per-service environment variables (ETP_DB_*, ETP_IAM_DB_*) — see configuration section

jdbcConsumers: Hibernate ddl-auto=validate with Flyway-managed schema (current platform and IAM pattern)
expectations: Consumers must use PostgreSQL-compatible SQL for migrations
UTC timezone recommended for timestamps (configured in current consumers)
PostgreSQL 17 Docker image matches repository compose files

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: Database name in JDBC URL path

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Default public unless consumer configures Hibernate default_schema

parameters.name: connection pool
parameters.description: Spring Boot HikariCP defaults; optional spring.datasource.hikari.* per consumer

parameters.name: Docker POSTGRES_DB
parameters.description: Initial database name when using official postgres image

dependencies.note: PostgreSQL is infrastructure. Registry dependencies[] is empty. Consumers connect via JDBC directly.
